seo.title: Bali Summer Program | Pacific Discovery
seo.description: Four weeks in Bali for college-aged travelers: food rescue and a mangrove clean-up in Sanur, Tabanan’s villages, surfing in Uluwatu, conservation on Nusa Penida, a yoga retreat in Ubud and a Mount Batur sunrise.

hero.headline: Four weeks of service, surf and volcanoes in Bali
hero.intro: Discover the Bali beyond the beaches. Give back in Sanur and Tabanan, learn to surf in Uluwatu, join a conservation project on Nusa Penida, reset at a yoga retreat in Ubud and watch the sun rise from Mount Batur, with free days at every stage to explore at your own pace.
hero.imageAlt: Group silhouetted on a leaning palm tree over the water at dusk

itinerary.heading: Week by week
itinerary.note: This is a guide to what you can expect to do on program. The order in which activities occur might vary. Itineraries are subject to change.

weeks.title: Service in Sanur
weeks.body:
We land in Denpasar and head to Sanur, a relaxed beach town on Bali’s east coast and our base for the first six days. After a day of orientation with our instructors, we get straight into service: a day packaging food with a local food rescue partner, getting surplus food to families who need it, and a day supporting the Bali Life Centre.

A free day lets you explore the seaside boardwalk, night market and beaches, and we finish our time in Sanur with a mangrove clean-up, protecting one of Bali’s most important coastal ecosystems.
weeks.imageAlt: Students learning dance moves in an open-air pavilion

weeks.title: Tabanan villages & Uluwatu surf
weeks.body:
We travel west to Tabanan, the rice bowl of Bali. Here we deliver food to local villages, visit temples that are still at the heart of community life, trek through the countryside and spend a morning working alongside local farmers before an evening dinner at Tabanan Palace. A free day lets you chase waterfalls, visit more temples or head to the beach.

Then we head south to Uluwatu, home to some of Bali’s most famous surf breaks, for surf lessons with a local surf school. A free day follows, with options to keep surfing, watch the Kecak Fire Dance at sunset or explore the cliff-top temples.
weeks.imageAlt: Group silhouetted on a leaning palm tree over the water at dusk

weeks.title: Nusa Penida conservation & Ubud
weeks.body:
We cross by fast boat to Nusa Penida, a rugged island off Bali’s southeast coast, for a three-day conservation project with a local environmental foundation, learning how local communities and conservationists work together to protect the island’s wildlife. A free day follows to snorkel, dive or look for manta rays in some of the clearest water in Indonesia.

Back on the mainland we settle into Ubud, Bali’s cultural heart. A day at a local eco farm shows how sustainable farming and Balinese traditions fit together, and a free day lets you try a batik class or silver making, or wander the art markets.
weeks.imageAlt: Two people standing in a stone temple gateway reflected in water

weeks.title: Yoga retreat & Mount Batur sunrise
weeks.body:
We settle into Dragonfly Village for a three-day yoga retreat, with sessions each day and time to rest, reflect and reset. Back in Ubud, a free afternoon lets you visit the Monkey Forest, go river rafting or explore the temples.

Our final days begin with what many students call the highlight of the program: we climb the active Mount Batur, camp near the summit and wake before dawn to watch the sun rise over Lake Batur and Mount Agung. Back in Ubud we reflect on the past four weeks and celebrate together before flying home from Denpasar.

day.heading: What a typical day looks like

notes.title: Free time
notes.body: Free days are built into every stage of the program so you can explore at your own pace, alongside time to catch up on laundry and rest.

notes.title: Phones & wifi
notes.body: We encourage flight mode so you stay present. Wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns.

notes.title: Fitness needed
notes.body: Medium activity level. Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. Expect surf lessons, trekking in Tabanan, hands-on service projects and an overnight hike up Mount Batur.

items.title: Service learning
items.body: Food rescue and the Bali Life Centre in Sanur, a mangrove clean-up, village food deliveries in Tabanan and a three-day conservation project on Nusa Penida.

items.title: Certificate of Completed Service Hours
items.body: You leave with a certificate documenting your service learning, and real experience to talk about in applications and interviews.

items.title: Optional college credit
items.body: Earn college credit through the University of Montana. 529 education funds can be used to pay for your credits and your Pacific Discovery program tuition.

faq.heading: Questions we get about this program

items.q: Do I need to know how to surf?
items.a: No. Surf lessons in Uluwatu are with a local surf school and suit first-timers as well as students who have surfed before.

items.q: How much free time is there?
items.a: Free days are built into every stage of the trip: in Sanur, Tabanan, Uluwatu, Nusa Penida and Ubud. Use them to keep surfing, snorkel with manta rays, chase waterfalls or explore at your own pace.

items.q: How fit do I need to be?
items.a: Anyone with average fitness and enthusiasm for the outdoors will be fine. You don’t need experience with any of the activities, but be ready for surf lessons, trekking, service projects and an overnight hike up Mount Batur.
Mostly hotels and hostels, plus Coliving Bali in Tabanan, a surf stay in Uluwatu, Dragonfly Village for the yoga retreat and one night camping near the summit of Mount Batur.

items.q: What is the yoga retreat like?
items.a: Three days at Dragonfly Village in Ubud, with yoga sessions each day and time to rest, reflect and reset after three busy weeks.

Tuition covers all in-country transport (private minivan and fast boat), accommodation, breakfast every day and many lunches and dinners, and the activities and entry fees in the itinerary. It doesn't cover international flights, visas, travel insurance, meals not listed as included, spending money, optional college credit or optional activities.
Meals are fresh, healthy and varied, from nasi goreng, satay and gado-gado to grilled fish and familiar favorites. Vegetarians and special diets are catered for.
Bali is tropical year-round and summer falls in the dry season (April to October). Expect days of 80–88°F, nights of 70–75°F and ocean temperatures of 79–82°F.

items.q: How much spending money should I bring?
items.a: About $100 a week for snacks, laundry, personal shopping and optional activities. It varies from student to student.

items.q: Can I stay in touch with home?
items.a: Yes. We encourage keeping phones on flight mode so you stay present, and wifi is available where we stay in cities and towns. There will also be a photo album that students and instructors can upload photos and video to, so parents and caregivers can stay up to date.

items.q: Do I need a passport or visa?
items.a: Your passport must be valid for more than 6 months after the program ends. All the information you need in regard to visas will be available in your student portal.

safety.heading: For parents: how we keep students safe

items.title: 24/7 Emergency Line
items.body: Parents, students and instructors can reach a real person at any hour. Every call is logged and passed to our on-call staff member by phone.

items.title: Wilderness First Aid & Live Risk Assessment
items.body: All our instructors hold Wilderness First Aid (WFA) certification and have extensive training in group leadership and risk management.

items.title: Accredited Safety Systems
items.body: Our safety systems are assessed and accredited by the Gap Year Association (USA), Year Out Group (UK) and OutdoorsMark (NZ). Students on Go Overseas voted us one of the top gap year providers for safety.

items.title: Insurance & Health
items.body: Comprehensive travel insurance is required, covering medical costs and emergency evacuation. Check vaccinations with your doctor, and pack a first-aid kit and any personal medication. Our instructors can't legally give students any medication.
